analysis: Margin-stratified ('pivotal vote') check, exploratory, no new data.
reference: Shu 2026, arXiv:2608.06940 - verification concentrates on single-vote-margin cases.

multiplicity_check.method: Permute failure labels within repository, recompute the MAXIMUM AUROC(u) across the three margin strata, 4000 draws.
multiplicity_check.reading: The best of three small strata reaches ~0.72-0.73 under the null, so neither observed best is remarkable. The winning stratum is also at opposite ends on the two benchmarks. Disagreement does not concentrate on close-call selections; the pivotal-vote pattern reported for code-review panels does not reproduce for selection margin here.

conclusion: Exploratory and negative. Selection margin itself barely predicts failure (0.504 / 0.594), and stratifying by it does not reveal a region where disagreement works. Reported so that the obvious reviewer question - 'did you look at the close calls?' - has an answer.
